question.worked_solution:
The "square of a difference" formula states that

$$
{a}^{2}-2ab+{b}^{2}=(a-b)^{2}.
$$

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

$$
36{x}^{2}-12x+1.
$$

First, we write both the quadratic term and the constant term as perfect squares:

$$
\begin{aligned}(6x)^{2}-12x+(1)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we factor a $2$ out of the linear term:

$$
\begin{aligned}(6x)^{2}-2(6x)+(1)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we write the middle parentheses $(6x)$ as a product of $6x$ and $1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(6x)^{2}-2(6x\cdot 1)+(1)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of difference formula with $a=6x$ and $b=1.$ This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}(6x-1)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
